{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
The choir director always said the bishop might visit any rehearsal. We sang every practice like it was a performance. After five years in the choir, the bishop visited exactly once—his first time ever attending a rehearsal. The director admitted he'd invented the threat. 'Excellence requires pressure,' he said.

CANDIDATE A:
The choir director told us the bishop would attend our Easter rehearsal, so we sang every run-through like a performance. The bishop came exactly as promised and praised how prepared we were. The director had simply passed along the real visit schedule.

CANDIDATE B:
My driving instructor insisted police frequently monitored that intersection with speed cameras. I drove precisely every time we passed. When I got my license, a cop friend said there had never been cameras there. The instructor believed invisible surveillance created careful drivers.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:41"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a figure of authority creating a false sense of pressure to elicit better performance, with the revelation that the threat was unfounded."}
